CausalChain: CLDN18.2 overexpression on gastric cancer cells -> Acidic and hypoxic tumor microenvironment suppresses immune function -> Conventional CAR-T cells show limited persistence and cytotoxicity -> Tunable upregulation of HK2/PFK1 enhances glycolytic capacity under stress -> CRISPRi-mediated partial knockdown of PD-1 and Tim-3 reduces inhibitory signaling -> Inducible CCR6 expression improves trafficking to tumor sites -> Real-time metabolic monitoring enables dynamic regulation -> Multifunctional CAR-T cells maintain function and persist -> Enhanced tumor cell lysis and therapeutic outcomes.
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that engineering CLDN18.2-specific CAR-T cells with an integrated, tunable metabolic module that selectively upregulates glycolytic enzymes HK2 and PFK1, combined with CRISPRi-mediated partial knockdown of inhibitory checkpoints (PD-1 and Tim-3) and inducible expression of the chemokine receptor CCR6, will enable these CAR-T cells to overcome the suppressive acidic and hypoxic tumor microenvironment in gastric cancer. By coupling these modifications with real-time metabolic monitoring, we aim to dynamically adjust CAR-T cell activity to maintain optimal energy production, ensure controlled activation and targeted trafficking, and ultimately achieve superior tumor cell lysis and therapeutic efficacy.
Abstract: In this study, we propose a next-generation immunotherapy strategy for gastric cancer by engineering multifunctional CLDN18.2-specific CAR-T cells with integrated tunable modules. Our design incorporates a controllable metabolic regulation system to selectively upregulate key glycolytic enzymes (HK2 and PFK1), thereby enhancing energy production under the acidic and hypoxic conditions of the tumor microenvironment. In parallel, we employ CRISPR-interference (CRISPRi) to achieve partial knockdown of inhibitory checkpoints (PD-1 and Tim-3), optimizing T cell persistence without risking uncontrolled activation. Additionally, inducible expression of the chemokine receptor CCR6 is introduced to improve targeted trafficking toward tumor sites. Real-time metabolic monitoring further supports dynamic adjustment of these modifications, ensuring CAR-T cell functionality and safety. This comprehensive approach aims to overcome microenvironmental challenges, leading to improved tumor cell lysis and therapeutic outcomes.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis combined enhanced glycolytic capacity through HK2/PFK1 upregulation, checkpoint knockdown, and CCR6 expression to overcome the tumor microenvironment. The revised hypothesis retains these key elements but introduces contemporary technological improvements for practical implementation: 1) It incorporates tunable regulatory systems (e.g., inducible gene expression) for both glycolytic enzyme upregulation and CCR6 expression to prevent potential overactivation or adverse metabolic effects, addressing concerns related to T cell exhaustion and safety. 2) It utilizes CRISPRi for partial, rather than complete, knockdown of inhibitory checkpoints to balance efficacy with safety. 3) It leverages real-time metabolic monitoring technologies to dynamically tailor CAR-T cell functions in response to environmental stresses. These refinements ensure that the hypothesis remains novel and logically coherent while enhancing its translational potential.
